headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of expanding generation capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, advocates for lower utility bills, Governor Spanberger (with amendments), Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially).
opponents: Data center industry, Dominion Energy (opposed some Governor's amendments).
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Legislation Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allows Dominion Energy to spend on burying distribution lines. The bill aims to shift capacity market costs, which have significantly increased, away from general ratepayers to large energy users like data centers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandated
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for public transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups, advocates for transparency.
opponents: Data center industry (may view it as singling them out or adding administrative burden).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption and provide greater transparency.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry (may face increased development costs and restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia Adds New Restrictions on Data Center Siting and Noise
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 153, to regulate data centers by requiring site assessments for noise and allowing localities to consider other environmental impacts. These measures aim to address community concerns regarding the rapid expansion of data centers in Virginia.
